Author: Virender Singh
Bench: Virender Singh

 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Jabalpur
 Criminal Revision No.3568/2021
 (Devendra Ku. Agarwal Vs. State of M.P
 Jabalpur, dated : 24-02-2022
 Shri Vijay Nayak, counsel for the petitio
 Shri Chandrapal Singh Parma, Public Prose
 respondent No.1-State.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that now the petitioner has surrendered and he is in jail.

He referred to the Vakalatnama filed by him received from the Superintendent, Central Jail,
Narmadapuram.
Relying on the statement of learned counsel for the petitioner, it is presumed that the petitioner is in jail.
Heard on admission.
Revision appears to be arguable, therefore, admitted for hearing.
2. Also heard on I.A.No.23230/2021 which is the first application under Section 397(1) of CrPC for suspension of sentence of the petitioner.

3. By way of present revision under Section 397/401 of CrPC, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and order dated 30.10.2021 passed in CRA No.134/2015 by the Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshangabad, District Hoshangabad whereby the judgment dated 23.07.2015 passed in Criminal Case No.1704/2010 by JMFC, Hoshangabad, District Hoshangabad has been upheld.

entities.text: Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshangabad, District Hoshangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:

Conviction under section Sentence to undergo 16(1)(A)(1) r/w 2(1-A) & R.I. for 6 fine of Default- R.I. Section 7(1) of Prevention of months Rs.1,000/- for 2 months Food Adulteration Act

sentences.text: 4. As informed by the ld. counsel for the petitioner, the fine amount has been deposited.

5. The grounds taken by the ld. counsel for the petitioner are that no standard for "Namkeen Sev" (a salted snack) has been prescribed in the Act and the FSL report does not state as to how the sample was adulterated or sub-standard.
There is no mention in the FSL report of existence of presence of starch in the sample.
The FSL report also does not say that the sample was injurious to health or was not fit for human consumption, therefore, the conviction recorded by both the Courts below is contrary to law.
6. The other grounds taken by the ld. counsel for the petitioner are that provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act has not been complied with.
The petitioner has been deprived from his valuable rights.
The compliance of the provision was mandatory and its non-compliance is fatal to the prosecution case.

Public Analyst has not been examined before the trial Court and lastly, it is submitted that witness of seizure has turned hostile, therefore, there are fair chances of the petitioner for his acquittal.
The revision would take time to be heard finally.

The petitioner is ready to furnish adequate surety and to abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Court, therefore, prayer is made to suspend the custodial sentence of the petitioner.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner referred to the judgment of this Court rendered in the case of Kanwarlal Vs State of M.P. reported in 2002 (4) M.P.H.T. 402 wherein this Court has held that when the Public Analyst's report does not say that Namkeen Sev was not upto the standard as prescribed for gram-flour (Besan) and foreign matter i.e. starch was present in it, the accused is entitled for acquittal.
8.

entities.text: Kanwarlal Vs State of M.P. reported in 2002 (4) M.P.H.T. 402
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While opposing the prayer, the ld. Public Prosecutor for the State has referred to the paragraphs 26, 27 and 28 of the judgment of the trial Court and submitted that trial Court has considered the grounds raised by the petitioner before this Court and has discarded them rightly.

The conviction of the petitioner is well founded,
therefore, the custodial sentence of the petitioner may not be suspended.

9. According to the prosecution case, suspecting the quality of "Namkeen-Sev", Food Inspector-Jagdish Prasad Lovewanshi collected sample from the shop of the petitioner on 08.09.2010 and following the due process, sent it for analysis.
After analyzing the same, the Public Analyst submitted the following report with the opinion that "the sample is adulterated".

The report is as under :
Sl. Quality Characteristics Name of Result Prescribed Standards No. Method of as per test used (a) Item A ......
(b) As per label declaration for proprietory foods.

1. Test for Added Colour Q.G.H.S Negative method 2. Test for salt ---"--- Positive 3. Test for Khesaridal ---"--- Positive Powder 4.

sentences.text: B.R. reading of ---"--- 60.2 extracted fat at 40oC 5. Visible extraneous ---"--- Nil Matter (Fungus/Insect)
10. Thus, the report clearly says that test for Khesaridal Powder was found positive in the sample and Khesaridal is banned or prohibited for human consumption.
The record shows that even after receiving notice (Exhibit-P/19), the petitioner never tried to avail his right for getting second sample analysised by the C.F.L.

The case of Kanwarlal (supra) has been considered by the trial Court in the paragraphs referred to by the ld. Public Prosecutor for the State and has rightly held that it is distinguishable on the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Nothing has been stated regarding presence of Khesaridal in the sample.
11. Considering the presence of such a prohibited article in the sample, the trial Court has rightly convicted the petitioner.

The other grounds taken by the petitioner are also not helpful to him,
therefore, on due consideration of the evidence produced by the prosecution and its appreciation by both the Courts below, no case for suspension of custodial sentence is made out.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, I.A. No.23230/2021 is dismissed.
12. However, looking to the period of sentence, liberty is granted to the petitioner to move an application for out of turn final hearing of this revision petition, if he wish to do so.
If such an application is filed, list the matter for final hearing at the earliest on any final hearing day falling immediately after filing of the application.
Otherwise, list as per the scheme of listing in vogue.
